cases.why: the Week Board goes back to hand-building its own title. This is the defect exactly as it was, and it is invisible in review: both copies read correctly, and the next change to the title edits one of them while the other looks like code nobody needed to touch. That is how the `@` separator survived on My Picks after being changed everywhere else, with a green suite and a diff that looked complete.

My Picks drops its call, so the helper exists, is tested, and is used by one page. A guard that says 'the title is built in one place' is satisfied by a helper nobody calls -- which is the shape Stage 3 closed with, when src/collect_agent_log.py was written, mutation-covered and had never run. Coverage has to be enumerated, not asserted.

the variant loses its display override and inherits .matchup-header's flex layout, whose 8px gap turns the words into flex items. 'NE at SEA' gets wider on My Picks with nobody deciding to -- a visual change riding along inside a refactor whose whole claim is that appearance did not move. Measured before and after precisely so this cannot happen quietly.

the variant starts altering the separator as well as the class list. One construction site producing two different sentences is the original defect in a subtler and harder-to-spot form: the count guard still passes, the call-site guard still passes, and the two pages disagree again. Only executing the function catches it.
the logos go back into the title as well as the bar, so every team shows its logo twice on one card.
the home end of the bar goes back to a bare abbreviation, so one side of the card has a logo and the other does not.
the logo carries the team as alt text, so a screen reader reads every team twice.
a logo ESPN will not serve stays on the card as a broken-image mark instead of hiding.
the bar's logos grow past the 20px the restyle set, and outweigh the abbreviations beside them.
on a phone the logo sits beside the abbreviation instead of above it, and the probability line narrows below the width its marker spacing was measured on.
